conventions.convention: Gaussian noising is Xσ = X0 + σZ with σ > 0, Z standard Gaussian and independent of X0. The prior may be singular and need not have bounded support.

The fixed-observation likelihood in the exact conditional-score identity is bounded, strictly positive and Borel, relative to a fixed sigma-finite observation measure; observation and noising noise are conditionally independent given the clean state.

Predictors are Borel and square-integrable under the smoothed marginal. Denoising-risk minimization additionally assumes a finite prior second moment; score-risk minimization does not. Uniqueness is modulo smoothed-marginal almost-everywhere equality.
The measurement score differentiates the likelihood averaged over the clean-state conditional law; evaluating the likelihood at the conditional mean is a separate approximation.

A finite schedule runs from k = N down to 1. Initialization, correction, sampling and projection have explicit failure branches and finite budgets; completed output is not automatically posterior-exact.
The finite-law sequence starts at m = 1. Weak convergence concerns bounded continuous test functions and does not assert equality at any finite index.

Finite reverse-kernel exactness requires the supplied terminal marginal and adjacent reverse conditional kernels, no projection, and almost-sure success. A realized finite particle measure is distinguished from the marginal law of a selected particle.

load_bearing.statement: For any Borel probability prior on R^d and σ > 0, Gaussian convolution has a positive continuously differentiable density and the displayed probability kernel is the clean-state conditional law. Its score is (mσ(x) − x)/σ². With finite prior second moment, mσ uniquely minimizes squared denoising risk; the score uniquely minimizes the stated score risk without that extra moment assumption. Under the stated bounded positive likelihood and conditional-independence hypotheses, the conditional score equals the prior score plus the logarithmic derivative of the averaged likelihood.

The procedure initializes from the supplied terminal reference law, applies the declared correction and reverse probability kernel for k = N,...,1, applies any declared projection and admissibility check, and returns the first failure status or completed x0. It makes no posterior-exactness claim unless terminal, transition and projection conditions are separately certified.

The diffusion prior score is the gradient of the log smoothed prior density; the measurement score is the gradient of the log likelihood averaged over the clean-state conditional law. Their sum is the conditional score. Likelihood evaluated at the clean-state conditional mean is a plug-in approximation.

The finite reverse-kernel interface and explicit finite-law example make no inference from finite evaluability to convergence, risk transfer or posterior exactness. The prerequisite is contextual; no stronger unrolling theorem is cited.

The InverseBench remark cites the distinction between exact scores and learned or plug-in approximations and expressly disclaims posterior-exactness and universal performance guarantees.

The coverage problem independently specifies variance-preserving noising and its reverse Euler chain. It does not identify that convention with additive Gaussian noising or claim exactness from a learned score or finite discretization.
